newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India GDRs hardly budge in dull trading.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India GDRs hardly budge in dull trading.

text.p: Indian global depository receipts (GDRs) showed few signs of life on Friday, taking their cue from a fairly moribund Bombay market.
"It's been very quiet. The market could come off another 50 to 100 points. The floor seems to be 3,600," one trader said.
The Bombay top share index finished at just over 3,700 points.
"It's a drifting market. It went up too quickly with speculators trying to front-run the funds. But funds are holding back a bit longer," the trader added.
Activity is also dampened by the wait for GDR issue by state-run overseas telecommunications monopoly Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd, whose roadshow is currently underway.
It is expected to be priced on March 24.

The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 0.54 points lower, wiping out almost all of Thursday's rise. The index finished 0.70 percent down at 76.03, while the premium over the local market dipped to 18.80 percent from Thursday's 19.66 percent.
In other Asian markets, the Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended up 1.22 points at 111.47. Prices were at a slight discount to the local market of 0.16 percent.
"Taiwan has been so strong over the last few weeks. There's been a bit of profit-taking, but we've managed to get a few more people in on the buy-side," one trader said.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended slightly higher at 56.70, up 1.02 points. The premium was 44.82 percent.
